title: La nouvelle agente de Fabrice  (Fabrice's New Agent)

segments.t: Sitting at her agency desk after a chaotic bluff involving a fake James Bond casting call, Andréa receives an unexpected phone call from star actor Fabrice Luchini. Amused by her daring tactics and grateful for her romantic encouragement, the eccentric actor announces that he wants her as his new agent, right as agency boss Hicham looks on in approval. Listen to the scene in French first. Don't worry about catching every word.
Allô?
Bonjour, Andréa. C'est Fabrice Luchini.
Bonjour, Fabrice. Vous allez bien?
Très bien. Je voulais juste vous dire...
J'ai rendez-vous avec elle ce soir.
C'est formidable, je suis vraiment contente pour vous.
Grâce à vous! Vous m'avez revigoré.
Je trouve ça drôle. Vous êtes une joueuse, et c'est rare.
Merci.
Ce serait un plaisir de les découvrir avec vous.
Merci pour votre appel, Fabrice.
Prenez soin de vous... Ma Nouvelle Agente.
À bientôt, Fabrice.
À bientôt.
Bravo, Martel.
Je savais que vous en étiez capable.
Let's walk through the phone call of Fabrice Luchini step by step.
Allô?
'Hello?' Andréa answers her mobile phone at the agency.
Bonjour, Andréa. C'est Fabrice Luchini.
'Hello, Andréa. This is Fabrice Luchini.' Fabrice identifies himself warmly.
Bonjour, Fabrice. Vous allez bien?
'Hello, Fabrice. Are you well?' Andréa uses the polite question form.
Très bien. Je voulais juste vous dire...
'Very well. I just wanted to tell you...' Listen for the expression meaning 'very', which leads naturally into 'to tell'.
J'ai rendez-vous avec elle ce soir.
'I have a date with her tonight.' Fabrice pairs the verb meaning 'I have' with the noun for 'evening'.
C'est formidable, je suis vraiment contente pour vous.
'That's wonderful, I am really happy for you.' The feminine adjective 'happy' agrees with Andréa.
Grâce à vous! Vous m'avez revigoré.
'Thanks to you! You have revitalized me.' Listen for the expression meaning 'have me', which leads naturally into 'revitalized'.
Je trouve ça drôle. Vous êtes une joueuse, et c'est rare.
'I find it funny. You are a gambler, and that is rare.' The key word here means 'find', paired with 'rare' to make the point clear.
Merci.
'Thank you.' Andréa accepts his flattering compliment.
Ce serait un plaisir de les découvrir avec vous.
'It would be a pleasure to discover them with you.' Fabrice pairs the verb meaning 'would be' with the noun for 'pleasure'.
Merci pour votre appel, Fabrice.
'Thank you for your call, Fabrice.' Andréa thanks him for reaching out directly.
Prenez soin de vous... Ma Nouvelle Agente.
'Take care of yourself... My New Agent.' The key word here means 'take', paired with 'agent' to make the point clear.
À bientôt, Fabrice.
'See you soon, Fabrice.' Andréa says goodbye to her prestigious new client.
À bientôt.
'Talk to you soon.' Fabrice returns the farewell before hanging up.
Bravo, Martel.
'Well done, Martel.' Hicham steps in to congratulate his daring agent.
Je savais que vous en étiez capable.
'I knew you were capable of it.' Hicham opens with the word for 'knew' and lands on 'capable' at the close. Now listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.

By winning over Fabrice Luchini with her boldness, Andréa saves her position at ASK and earns the hard-won respect of new majority shareholder Hicham Janowski. We'll pick up right after this in the next scene.
